title: Justin Welsh: Optimize for time, not scale, and play the long game
summary: Justin Welsh explains why he built a one-person business around time, family and experiences rather than scale. He covers anti-goals, shutting down a working community, course design and pricing, borrowing proven formats to grow on Twitter, and acting today instead of perfecting.

principles.text: Treat building a brand as a decades-long journey, so short-term dips in engagement don't derail pivots.
principles.quote: I think of this as like a decades-long journey not like what happens on Thursday compared to Wednesday is is irrelevant to me

principles.text: Stack transferable skills (action, clear communication, ego control) so you can go in any direction with confidence.
principles.quote: getting one percent better at 17 different things all the time and uh you blink and suddenly you're a much more well-rounded marketer content creator business person

principles.text: Use anti-goals: decide what you don't want to do, then cut it. Narrowing niche and raising rates opens time that finds new revenue.
principles.quote: an idea of like an anti-goal isn't like this is the goal I want to achieve it's like this is the stuff I don't want to do next year

principles.text: Shut down even a profitable product if it conflicts with your values, and don't automatically refill the freed time.
principles.quote: my goal wasn't to like see a free Gap and fill it yeah that would have defeated the purpose of what I was doing

principles.text: Define riches as time, friends, family and experiences; once income is enough, you don't need to 2x or 5x it.
principles.quote: I don't need to scale I don't need to 2x I don't need to 5x like if it just stays consistent for the next 10 to 20 years I'll be thrilled

principles.text: Price a course as an impulse buy that still feels worth using, and treat it as a Trojan horse for a later premium product.
principles.quote: it's affordable enough to make it an Impulse buy but it's expensive enough where like you don't really want to waste 150 bucks
